questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence. It was difficult to accommodate the avariciousness of the people.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence.
It was difficult to accommodate the avariciousness of the people.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1.

Key Points

  • The word "avariciousness" means extreme greed for wealth or material gain. (लोभ)
    • Example: The avariciousness of the businessman led him to exploit his employees.
  • "Generosity" refers to the quality of being kind and generous, often involving giving freely. (उदारता)
    • Example: Her generosity knew no bounds as she donated a large sum to charity.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of "avariciousness" is "generosity".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Criticism (आलोचना): The expression of disapproval of someone or something based on perceived faults or mistakes.
    • Example: Her criticism of the new policy was harsh but fair.
  • Hatred (घृणा): Intense dislike or ill will.
    • Example: His hatred for injustice was evident in his passionate speeches.
  • Envy (ईर्ष्या): A feeling of discontented or resentful longing aroused by someone else's possessions, qualities, or luck.
    • Example: She felt envy towards her friend's success.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. He has written a best-selling novel.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

He has written a best-selling novel.

options.text: A best-selling novel was being written by him
options.html: A best-selling novel was being written by him

options.text: A best-selling novel has been written by him
options.html: A best-selling novel has been written by him

options.text: A best-selling novel was written by him
options.html: A best-selling novel was written by him

options.text: A best-selling novel would have been written by him
options.html: A best-selling novel would have been written by him

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.
 

Key Points

  • The active sentence “He has written a best-selling novel” is in the present perfect tense (has written). 
  • When converting to the passive voice, the tense remains the same:
  • has written → has been written

So, the correct passive construction is: A best-selling novel has been written by him.

Additional Information

Why others are incorrect:

  • Option 1: was being written → past continuous (wrong tense)
  • Option 3: was written → simple past (tense changes)
  • Option 4: would have been written → conditional perfect (changes meaning)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. P) her face Q) I have R) for a year S) not seen
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
P) her face
Q) I have
R) for a year
S) not seen
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option (4) i.e. QSPR
Key Points
  • The sentence begins with the subject "I have," which is correctly indicated by part (Q).
  • Following the subject, "not seen" (S) continues the logical sequence, making it clear what the subject has not done.
  • The next part, "her face," (P) provides the object that the subject has not seen.
  • Ending with, "for a year" (R) completes the sentence by stating the duration.
Therefore, the correct answer is QSPR.
Additional Information
  • Option 1 (PQRS): This option starts with "her face I have not seen for a year," which disrupts the logical flow and structure of the sentence.
  • Option 2 (PSQR): This option starts with "her face not seen I have for a year," which creates an incorrect and confusing structure.
  • Option 3 (SPQR): This option starts with "not seen her face I have for a year," which is awkward and grammatically incorrect.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word from the following sentence. Barren "Can you believe how much traffic there is today?", grumbled Tom, glancing at the congested road ahead.

  • "Congested" refers to an area that is overcrowded or filled to excess, often causing delays or blockages. (भीड़-भाड़ वाला)
    • Example: The congested streets made it difficult to drive through the city during rush hour.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'Barren' is 'Congested'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Congested.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Believe (विश्वास करना): Accept something as true; feel sure of the truth of.
    • Example: He couldn't believe his eyes when he saw the surprise party.
  • Grumbled (बड़बड़ाना ): Complain or protest about something in a bad-tempered but typically muted way.
    • Example: She grumbled about the long wait at the doctor's office.
  • Glancing (झांकना): Taking a brief or hurried look.
    • Example: He kept glancing at his watch during the meeting.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate idiom for the given group of words. A time when money might unexpectedly be needed
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the given group of words.
A time when money might unexpectedly be needed
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1.

Key Points

  • The idiom "a rainy day" refers to a time when money might unexpectedly be needed. (मुश्किल समय के लिए बचत)
    • Example: It's always wise to save some money for a rainy day.
  • "A raw deal" means being treated unfairly. (अन्यायपूर्ण व्यवहार)
    • Example: She felt she got a raw deal when she was passed over for the promotion.
  • "A rash of something" refers to a large number of unpleasant events of the same type happening within a short period. (घटनाओं की बाढ़)
    • Example: There has been a rash of burglaries in our neighborhood recently.
  • "A rap over the knuckles" means a mild reprimand or scolding. (हल्की फटकार)
    • Example: The teacher gave him a rap over the knuckles for being late.
  • Hence, we can infer that the most appropriate idiom for a time when money might unexpectedly be needed is "a rainy day".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • A raw deal (अन्यायपूर्ण व्यवहार): Being treated unfairly.
    • Example: She felt she got a raw deal when she was passed over for the promotion.
  • A rash of something (घटनाओं की बाढ़): A large number of unpleasant events of the same type happening within a short period.
    • Example: There has been a rash of burglaries in our neighborhood recently.
  • A rap over the knuckles (हल्की फटकार): A mild reprimand or scolding.

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A.The door of the flat was ajar. B.The taxi stopped. C.Mr. Satterthwaite flung himself out and raced up the stone stairs to the second floor like a young athlete. D.He pushed it open, and the great voice welcomed him.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful
and coherent paragraph.
A.The door of the flat was ajar.
B.The taxi stopped.
C.Mr. Satterthwaite flung himself out and raced up the stone stairs to the second floor like a young athlete.
D.He pushed it open, and the great voice welcomed him.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option (3) i.e. BCAD
Key Points
  • The paragraph begins with "The taxi stopped," which is correctly indicated by part (B).
  • Following this, "Mr. Satterthwaite flung himself out and raced up the stone stairs to the second floor like a young athlete" (C) continues the logical sequence, describing the actions following the stopping of the taxi.
  • The next part, "The door of the flat was ajar," (A) provides a visual detail that Mr. Satterthwaite encounters as he reaches the flat.
  • Ending with, "He pushed it open, and the great voice welcomed him" (D) completes the process of entering the flat and being greeted.
Therefore, the correct answer is BCAD.
Additional Information
  • Option 1 (BACD): This option starts with the door being ajar before the taxi stops, which is logically inconsistent.
  • Option 2 (ABCD): This option starts with the door being ajar, which disrupts the narrative flow by placing a later detail first.
  • Option 4 (DCBA): This option starts with the voice welcoming, then goes backwards, which misarranges the sequence of actions.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. He wrote an inspiring speech for the event.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
He wrote an inspiring speech for the event.

options.text: An inspiring speech was being written by him for the event.
options.html: An inspiring speech was being written by him for the event.

options.text: An inspiring speech was written by him for the event.
options.html: An inspiring speech was written by him for the event.

options.text: An inspiring speech is written by him for the event.
options.html: An inspiring speech is written by him for the event.

options.text: An inspiring speech has been written by him for the event.
options.html: An inspiring speech has been written by him for the event.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.
 
Key Points
  • Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
  • In the active voice, the sentence is: "He wrote an inspiring speech for the event."
  • To convert to passive voice: Place the object "an inspiring speech" at the beginning.
  • Change the active verb form "wrote" to "was written" (past simple passive).
  • Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "him."
  • Ensure the phrase "for the event" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.
 
Correct Sentence: "An inspiring speech was written by him for the event."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "An inspiring speech was being written by him for the event." – Incorrect tense (past continuous passive).
  • Option 3: "An inspiring speech is written by him for the event." – Incorrect tense (present simple passive).
  • Option 4: "An inspiring speech has been written by him for the event." – Incorrect tense (present perfect passive).

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'indifferent'.
 
Key Points
  • The passage describes Federico Ardila-Mantilla as a student who was not performing well in most subjects except for math.
  • The word "indifferent" accurately reflects his lack of engagement or interest in other subjects, which aligns with his overall poor school performance.
  • Other options such as "apprehensive", "apologetic", and "excellent" do not appropriately capture the context of his academic indifference in subjects other than math.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 3'.
 
Complete Passage: The mathematician Federico Ardila-Mantilla grew up in Colombia, an indifferent student but gifted in math. He was failing most of his classes at his high school in Bogotá when someone encouraged him to apply to MIT. He had not heard of the school. To his surprise, he got in, and he went on scholarship. Mathematically, he did well. One of his professors, an acid-tongued theoretician known to liken his audience to a herd of cows, routinely tucked 'open' math problems into homework assignments, without telling the students. These had never been solved by anyone. Ardila solved one. He went on to receive his bachelor's and Ph.D. in math from MIT. But his academic experience was also one of isolation. Part of it had to do with his own shyness. Part of it was cultural. As a Latino, he was very much in the minority in the department, and he did not feel comfortable in American mathematical spaces. No one had tried to explicitly exclude him, yet he felt alone. In math, collaborating with others opens up new kinds of learning and thinking. But in his nine years at MIT, Ardila worked with others only twice.
 
Additional Information
  • Apprehensive (सशंकित): "Apprehensive" means anxious or fearful about something, which does not fit the context of discussing a lack of academic engagement.
  • Apologetic (क्षमाप्रार्थी): "Apologetic" means showing regret or remorse, which does not align with the context of the passage.
  • Excellent (उत्कृष्ट): "Excellent" means extremely good, which does not reflect the poor academic performance described.

Key Points
